verdict.justification: Both deliverables correctly prioritize the approved 21-day notice over the unapproved 84-day proposal and clearly distinguish recommendations from authorized actions. A provides the more executable continuity strategy: its quantified last-time buy, early mould-ahead, dated tooling release, separate development streams, and explicit integration allowance connect the negotiation asks to actual production coverage. B materially weakens its timeline by calling March–April 2027 a four-to-five-month electronics schedule from October 23, while subsequently scheduling development kickoff by Day 21 and retaining the same completion dates. B also constrains its acceptable pre-build to the initial 21-day surplus even when negotiating an extension, overlooking the larger inventory bridge that A develops from LPI’s excess capacity. A is more candid and useful about failure conditions, including tooling delays, insufficient bridge coverage, and the unresolved distinction between lamp units and sets. A would benefit from substantial compression to meet the requested executive-document length, but its stronger operational arithmetic and negotiation roadmap outweigh that presentation weakness.

decisive_issues.issue: Electronics completion dates do not match the stated four-to-five-month duration from the assumed Day-0 start.
The acceptable fallback unnecessarily limits pre-build to the initial notice-period surplus despite assuming an extension.
decisive_issues.quote: acceptable: bridge to 15-Jan-2027 plus a pre-build at the upper end of the 480–1,170 range, then LPI electronics-only supply to Apr-2027

decisive_issues.issue: The proposed BATNA remains dependent on a further agreement with LPI rather than clearly separating independent fallback actions from negotiated support.
decisive_issues.quote: Hence the BATNA is only as strong as the buffer and extension we can secure

decisive_issues.issue: Provides a concrete mould-ahead mechanism that enables tooling transfer without immediately ending LPI assembly.
decisive_issues.quote: LPI moulds the plastic components for the full LTB in the first four weeks, then releases the tools on Day 28 (20 Nov 2026) while it continues electronics and final assembly to Day 84.

decisive_issues.issue: Explicitly identifies a potentially decisive units-versus-sets capacity ambiguity and requires prompt escalation.
decisive_issues.quote: If LPI's 1,500/2,500 capacity means individual lamps and not sets, the 4,200-set floor needs 8,400 lamps, which exceeds 84 days at 2,500 lamps/month (≈7,000).
